title: The Empty Bench
synopsis: On the Brooklyn Bridge, Eleanor's bench waits under the first stone tower.
But the brass bird is gone.
Someone is following Eleanor's trail, one step ahead of you.
goal: Find out when the brass bird was taken, what it looks like, and who was there.

options.label: Before 9:30 AM
options.feedback: The prints are in the paint. Was there paint before 9:30?

options.label: After 11:30 AM
options.feedback: After 11:30 the paint was dry. Can a boot print stay in dry paint?

notes: Letter: the park's wet paint sign and the painter's line. The star prints are pressed into the paint, so the thief came while it was wet: 9:30 to 11:30. This window clears Otto in Case 06 (he was on the 9:30 ferry).

clueInputs.note: The tin note: the bench under the first stone tower.
The same star prints as at Grand Central.

learning.objective: 페인트 안내문의 시간(painted at 9:30, dry at 11:30)을 읽고, 젖은 페인트에 발자국이 찍힌 시간대를 추론한다.
expressions: This bench was painted at 9:30 AM.
The paint takes two hours to dry.

play.title: Wet Paint
story: You walk the bridge to the first stone tower.
There is the bench. But the brass bird is gone!
Only four screw holes, and star prints pressed into green paint.
play.letterIntro: A sign on the bench says:
play.letter:
WET PAINT
This bench was painted at 9:30 AM.
The paint takes two hours to dry.
Please do not touch it until 11:30 AM.
Painter's note: I painted around the little brass bird.
play.question: The star prints are pressed into the wet paint. When was the bird taken?
hints: When did the paint go on? When was it dry?
A boot can only leave a print while the paint is wet.
play.successMessage: You found when the bird was taken!
transition: The bird was still there at 9:30. The painter painted around it.
Someone in star boots took it before 11:30.
"The same stars as at Grand Central!" Maya says.

clue.title: Prints in Wet Paint
clue.note: The bird was taken while the paint was wet, between 9:30 and 11:30 on Sunday morning.

evidence.name: The Wet Paint Sign
evidence.description: The park's sign on the bench, with star prints in the green paint.
evidence.inscription: Painted at 9:30 AM. Dry at 11:30 AM.

play.evidenceLinkLine: The same five little stars as the print at Grand Central.

discovery.title: ONE STEP AHEAD
discovery.detail: Someone heard the tin note and came here first. Their boots have stars.

options.label: The bird standing on both feet
options.feedback: Its wings are open. But the tag says one foot is up.
options.altText: a small brass songbird with its wings wide open, standing on both feet, its beak open

options.label: The bird with one foot up
options.altText: a small brass songbird with its wings wide open, one foot lifted and its beak open

options.label: The bird with folded wings
options.feedback: One foot is up. But the tag says its wings are wide open.
options.altText: a small brass songbird with its wings folded, one foot lifted, its beak open

notes: A picture choice with the names hidden: Eleanor's tag names three things (wings wide open, one foot up, beak open); each wrong bird misses one of them. The right bird is the evidence picture ev_brass_bird; the wrong ones are drawn from it.
The same three pictures come back in Case 11 M2, on Dexter's studio shelf.

clueInputs.note: The brass bird carries the first three notes.
The bird was taken while the paint was wet.

learning.objective: 놋쇠 꼬리표의 세 특징(wings wide open, one foot up, beak open)을 읽고 맞는 새 그림을 고른다.
expressions: One foot is up, as if it dances.

play.title: The Missing Bird
story: Under the bench, a small brass tag is still screwed on.
The thief did not see it.
"Now we know what the bird looks like," Maya says.
play.letter:
Here sits my brass bird.
Its wings are wide open.
One foot is up, as if it dances.
Its beak is open to sing the first three notes of my song.
play.question: Which one is Eleanor's brass bird?
hints: The tag gives three things: the wings, the feet and the beak.
Check all three on each bird.
play.successMessage: Now you know Eleanor's brass bird!
transition: Wings open, one foot up, beak open to sing.
If you ever see this bird again, you will know it.
A painter waves from the railing. "I saw someone this morning!"

clue.title: The Dancing Bird
clue.value: WINGS OPEN · ONE FOOT UP · BEAK OPEN
clue.note: Eleanor's brass bird dances on one foot, its wings wide open.

evidence.name: Eleanor's Brass Bird
evidence.description: Eleanor's brass bird, as her tag tells it. Someone took it from the bench.
evidence.inscription: Its beak is open to sing the first three notes of my song.

discovery.title: THE DANCING BIRD
discovery.detail: The thief has the first half of the song now. Remember this bird.

notes: Letter: the painter's note about an old man at nine. He fixes clocks: Otto, seen at Grand Central (Case 02). A red herring cleared in Case 06.

clueInputs.note: Otto was at Grand Central too, looking at the clock.

learning.objective: 화가의 메모(a magnifying glass, he fixes clocks)에서 노인의 직업 단어를 만든다.
expressions: A person who makes and fixes clocks

play.title: The Man with the Toolbox
story: The painter hands you a note.
"I wrote it down," he says. "He was a strange old man."
play.letter:
At nine, an old man sat on this bench.
He wore a leather apron and carried a toolbox.
A little magnifying glass sat on his forehead.
He looked at the brass bird. He said he fixes clocks.
A person who makes and fixes clocks has one job name.
play.question: What is the old man's job?
hints: What does the old man fix?
Put two words together: what he fixes, and a person who makes things.
play.successMessage: You know the old man's job!
transition: A clockmaker with a toolbox and bushy eyebrows.
"Otto Brandt!" Maya says. "He was at Grand Central too."
But Otto came at nine. The paint went on at 9:30.

feedback.PAINTER: The painter wrote this note. What does the old man fix?
feedback.WATCHMAKER: Close! But the note says he fixes clocks.

clue.title: The Man with the Toolbox
clue.note: An old clockmaker looked at the bird at nine, before the paint. Was it Otto?

evidence.name: The Painter's Note
evidence.description: The bridge painter's note about the old man at the bench.
evidence.inscription: At nine, an old man with a toolbox looked at the brass bird.

lines.text: Otto said Eleanor taught his grandfather.
So he knows about the bird.
But does he have star boots?

discovery.title: THE CLOCKMAKER
discovery.detail: Otto Brandt was here at nine. Where was he after 9:30?

notes: Eleanor's spare box under the bench, missed by the thief. Its word is what shines on the ceiling of the great hall of trains (the rubbing, Case 01). Inside: her spare note, the one that leads to Rosa in Case 08.

clueInputs.note: The great hall of trains: its stars are painted on the ceiling.
The bird is gone, but Eleanor left a spare.

learning.objective: 'what shines on the ceiling of the great hall of trains'를 읽고 첫 번째 단서(painted stars)를 떠올려 글자를 맞춘다.
expressions: what shines on the ceiling of the great hall of trains

play.title: Eleanor's Spare Box
story: Behind the brass tag is a tiny box with five letter rings.
A line is written on the lid.
play.letter:
Clever reader!
My little box opens with a word:
what shines on the ceiling of the great hall of trains.
play.question: Spell the word that opens Eleanor's spare box.
hints: Think of your first clue: the great hall of trains.
What is painted on its green ceiling? More than one!
transition: Inside is a folded note from 1926.
"If my bird is lost, my song still lives," Maya reads.
"My family plays it on strings, with a bow."
play.orderFeedback: The five tiles fit. What is painted on the ceiling? More than one.

evidence.name: Eleanor's Spare Note
evidence.description: A note from Eleanor's spare box under the bench.
evidence.inscription: If my bird is lost, my song still lives. My family plays it on strings, with a bow. Find the one who plays it.

ending.text: Someone heard the tin note and came first.
ending.speaker: maya_chen

ending.text: Someone in star boots, while the paint was wet.
And Otto Brandt was here at nine.
ending.speaker: maya_chen

ending.text: Far below, a ferry sails toward the Statue of Liberty.
Who is racing you to the Lark?

hook: Someone is one step ahead on Eleanor's trail. Is it Otto the clockmaker?

learningGoal.title: Reading times: at 9:30, two hours, until
learningGoal.titleKo: 시간 읽기: at 9:30, two hours, until

objectives: Find out when the bird was taken.
Find out what the bird looks like.
intro: The Brooklyn Bridge. Stone towers, steel wires and the wind.
Below, boats sail on the East River.
Eleanor's brass bird should be on a bench here.
play.caseSummary: The brass bird is gone. Star prints in wet paint show when: between 9:30 and 11:30. Eleanor's tag tells what the bird looks like. A clockmaker sat on the bench at nine. Eleanor's spare box opened with STARS. Her family plays her song on strings.

notes: Act 1's turning point: the trail is no longer safe; someone who heard the tin note is ahead.
The 9:30 to 11:30 window (s4_ep04_c1) clears Otto in Case 06. Eleanor's spare note (s4_ep04_e4) leads to the violinist in Case 08.
